mappings.title:

- Click Pay Now and read every option offered in the modal.

- Open a plan carrying more than one overdue schedule.
- Choose Pay Overdue and check the offered amount against the sum of the overdue schedules.
- Try to type a larger amount.

[New] Pay Now - Pay Total Balance equals the overdue amount plus every pending installment of the plan.
- Open a plan that has both overdue schedules and pending future schedules.
- Choose Pay Total Balance and compare the amount with overdue + pending.
- Pay it in full and check the plan.

- Pay a custom amount smaller than that schedule's amount.
- Check the schedule's paid amount and its status.

[New] Custom Payment is always applied starting from the beginning of the schedule sequence (earliest unsettled schedule first), never to a later schedule the user might expect.
- Open a plan with several unsettled schedules.
- Pay a custom amount that covers about two schedules.
- Check which schedules absorbed the money and in what order.

[New] Custom Payment exactly equal to the total overdue clears all overdue schedules and leaves nothing spilling onto upcoming schedules (boundary).
- Open a plan with a known overdue total.
- Pay a custom amount exactly equal to that total.
- Check that no future schedule shows any part payment.

[New] Installments section status vocabulary - a schedule whose payment has been fully received is shown as Success.
- Let a scheduled charge run successfully (or collect it via Pay Now).
- Read the status column for that installment row.

[New] Installments section status vocabulary - a schedule for which only part of the money has been received is shown as Partial.
- Collect less than the full scheduled amount against one future schedule.
- Read the status column and the amounts for that row.

- Make a successful payment from the Pay Now modal.
- Check that the receipt view appears without the user having to hunt for it, and that it matches the payment.

[New] A cash / Pay Now receipt created from a payment plan cannot be edited (final BA decision - edits are not allowed, only deletion).
- Open a cash receipt created from Pay Now on a payment plan.
- Try to change its amount or any other field.

[New] Deleting a cash receipt that had settled ONE schedule sends that schedule back to Pending when its scheduled date has not yet passed.
- Pay one future schedule in advance with a cash receipt.
- Delete that receipt before the schedule's date arrives.
- Check the schedule's status and the plan balance.

[New] Deleting a cash receipt whose settled schedule's date has ALREADY passed sends that schedule to Overdue instead of Pending.
- Pay a schedule with a cash receipt and let its scheduled date pass.
- Delete the receipt.
- Check that the schedule comes back as Overdue and is counted in the overdue total.

[New] Deleting one cash receipt that had settled SEVERAL schedules reverses every one of them, each to Pending or Overdue depending on its own date.
- Make a large advance cash payment that settles several schedules, some past-dated and some future-dated.
- Delete that single receipt.
- Check each affected schedule separately.

[New] Deleting an EARLIER cash receipt while a LATER receipt also exists only reverses the earlier receipt's own schedules - the later receipt and its schedules stay intact.
- Create a receipt for one schedule, then a second receipt for a following schedule.
- Delete the first (earlier) receipt.
- Check both the reversed schedule and the schedule settled by the later receipt.

[New] A plan is completed once the TOTAL payment has been received, and the plan status must automatically become Inactive.
- Take a plan with an end date and collect the whole remaining balance.
- Check the plan status right after the last money is received.

[New] A plan is also completed when its END DATE has passed, and the plan status must automatically become Inactive at that point.
- Take an active plan whose end date is about to pass.
- Let the end date pass.
- Check the plan status.

- Try to change the payment method on each.

- Confirm no attempt occurs during the configured night window.

mappings.title: [New] Confirmation Number in the Payment Successful letter is filled with the payment number generated for the credit-card transaction.
[New] Confirmation Number in the Payment Successful letter matches the payment number shown on Transaction Tracking for the same charge.
[New] A Pay Now credit-card payment also produces a Payment Successful letter carrying that Pay Now transaction payment number.
[New] Card Expiry reminder always prints the LAST day of the expiry month as the card expiry date.
[New] Card Expiry reminder last-day rule is correct for 31-day, 30-day, 28-day and leap-year February expiry months.
[New] A card is not treated as expired before the last day of its expiry month, so scheduled charges before that day still run.
[New] Every payment-plan notification and reminder e-mail is sent from the clinic e-mail setup address.
[New] Changing the clinic e-mail setup changes the sender of subsequently generated payment-plan e-mails.
[New] Payment-plan e-mails use the e-mail setup of the clinic the plan belongs to when more than one clinic is configured.

[New] A default letter template exists for each of the seven payment-plan events: Payment Successful, Payment Failed, Payment Plan Setup, Payment Plan Status Change, Payment Due, Card Expiry and Payment Plan Agreement.
[New] The seven payment-plan default templates are applied to all databases by default, without any manual setup.
[New] Each payment-plan default template provides both the Email and the Text layout where the event supports both channels.
[New] Clicking Agree & Continue on the Agreement sends the agreement to the patient by e-mail when the agreement event is set in the notification preference.
[New] The agreement e-mail carries the agreement document itself, showing the terms the patient accepted.
[New] Confirm whether the agreement e-mail must also carry a body text along with the agreement document, and what that body text should say.

mappings.title: [New] The agreement e-mail is only sent when the Agreement event is enabled in the notification preference.
[New] The generated agreement document is stored at the patient level and can be re-opened from the Agreement button.
[New] Updating the payment plan clears the previous agreement document and a new agreement is shown.
[New] The regenerated agreement carries the UPDATED plan terms.
[New] If the regenerated agreement is skipped after a plan update, it can be re-opened later from the Agreement button with the new terms.
[New] No surcharge line or field appears in any payment-plan notification or reminder letter, because surcharge is deferred to a separate ER.
[New] The receipt generated from a payment plan payment shows no surcharge field or column.
[New] The Payment Plan Agreement document contains no surcharge clause, field or amount.
[New] The Reconciliation Preference field is visible on the patient payment plan and auto-populates to "No" (Do not reconcile) on a new plan.
[New] The Reconciliation Preference offers exactly three options: Do not reconcile, Reconcile to self/guarantor only, and Reconcile to family members balance.
[New] Do not reconcile: the payment creates an Open Credit that is NOT applied to any balance.
[New] Reconcile to self / guarantor only: the Open Credit is applied when the guarantor and the patient are the same person.
[New] Reconcile to self / guarantor only: nothing is reconciled when the guarantor is a different person from the patient.
[New] The "Reconcile to family members balance" option is available only when Patient Payment From is set to Immediate Guarantor / Patient / Dependent Only.
[New] The family reconciliation option is not available when Patient Payment From is not set to Immediate Guarantor / Patient / Dependent Only.
[New] Reconcile to family members balance: the Open Credit is applied across the guarantor and the dependents as allowed by the "Allow Payment From" client setting.
[New] The user can change the Reconciliation Preference at any time, including in the middle of a running plan.
[New] A changed Reconciliation Preference applies to reconciliation performed after the change, not retrospectively to Open Credits already processed.
[New] Switching the preference from a reconcile option back to Do not reconcile stops further automatic application.
[New] The chosen Reconciliation Preference is stored with the plan and survives reopening, refreshing and re-login.
[New] Auto reconciliation applies the Open Credit to charges by Date of Service, earliest first.
[New] Auto reconciliation follows pure Date of Service order with NO patient-first or guarantor-first priority.
[New] When reconciling a guarantor or dependent balance the system checks that the Date of Service falls inside that person from–to date range.
[New] Charges whose Date of Service falls outside the guarantor/dependent from–to range are skipped and the next eligible charge is taken instead.
[New] Boundary: a charge whose Date of Service is exactly the guarantor/dependent FROM date is reconciled.
[New] Boundary: a charge whose Date of Service is exactly the guarantor/dependent TO date is reconciled.
[New] Only the patient-responsible amount is reconciled by auto reconciliation.
[New] An amount that is entirely pending with insurance is never reconciled by auto reconciliation.
[New] Auto reconciliation is carried out by the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler.
[New] If the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler has not run, the Open Credit stays unapplied even when the preference is set to reconcile.
[New] Zero balance: when there is nothing outstanding to reconcile the Open Credit stays fully unapplied.
[New] Open Credit larger than the total outstanding balance: the leftover amount stays unapplied.
[New] Open Credit smaller than the earliest charge: the earliest-DOS charge is partially applied and the rest stays outstanding.
[New] End-to-end: a successful plan charge creates an Open Credit that the scheduler applies to the earliest eligible balances per the chosen preference.
[New] Self / guarantor only: dependents balances are never touched even when the patient has nothing outstanding.
[New] The reconciliation preference does not change how the payment itself is collected or how the receipt is created.
[New] The patient statement shows payment plans associated with the patient or their contact guarantor only.
[New] The patient statement does not show payment plans of a guarantor who is not the patient contact guarantor.
[New] Guarantor statement with Family Billing OFF shows payment plans associated with the patients and the guarantor.
[New] Guarantor statement with Family Billing ON shows payment plans associated with the guarantor, the dependents and the patients.
[New] With Family Billing TRUE, both the patient and the guarantor statements include ALL linked patient/guarantor payment plan information.
[New] With Family Billing FALSE, the statements show payment plan information only for directly linked patients/guarantors.
[New] Toggling Family Billing changes the payment plan information included on the next generated statement.
[New] Statement payment plan information matches the plan screen values for every listed plan.
[New] Statements remain correct for a patient or guarantor who has no payment plan at all.
[New] Reconciliation and statement behaviour stay consistent for a plan whose preference was changed mid-schedule.
